flawed_step: 0037 | The conclusion that sending the closest ambulance is globally optimal is not established and is false even in the proof's simplified model.
counterexample: For a first incident at t in (1/2, 5/8), sending a left-side ambulance has expected two-call cost t+1/4, while sending the closest ambulance C has expected cost (1-t)+1/2=3/2-t. Since t+1/4 < 3/2-t in this interval, the non-closest dispatch is better.
assessment_summary: Steps 15–35 only compare closest-dispatch with the rigid policy of always dispatching A first. They do not consider policies conditioned on the exact first-call location. Such a policy improves on closest-dispatch, so the global-optimality claim in step 37 fails.
